simple.meaning: עָרַף (ʻâraph) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to droop ; hence, to drip.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 2 times in Deuteronomy, beginning at Deuteronomy 32:2. The surrounding contexts include Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to עָרַף (H6201) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: עָרַף (ʻâraph) / H6201 is traced through Deuteronomy 32:2, Deuteronomy 33:28 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H6201. araph II. [ עָרַף ] verb drip, drop (compare Arabic lade out water with the hand (as with ladle), compare Phoenician ערפת portico (whence rain drips ) see Hoffm Abh. d. GGW xxxvi, May, 1889, 12 f. ; compare also Arabic upper-room ; ענן מערף Ecclus 43:22 the dropping of a cloud , Assyrian irpu, irpitu, cloud(s) ); — Qal Imperfect 3masculine plural יַעַרְפוּטָֿ֑ל שָׁמָיו Deut 33:28 his heavens drop dew ; figurative, of speech, intransitive, לִקְחִי כַּמָּטָר יַעֲרֹף 32:2 let my teaching drop like the rain (|| אִמְרָתִי כַּטַּל תִּזַּל ). — compare רָעַף .
